# questions.md — questions generated by contradiction

These are outputs of Cycle 1, not a preface to it. Each traces to a specific contradiction or survivor. Ordered by `importance × uncertainty × generativity`, which is also the Cycle 2 agenda.

---

## Q-01 — Is there a formalism for constitution without a pre-given total state space? `[HIGHEST PRIORITY]`

**From:** `contradictions.md` K-005, `survivors.md` S-05, S-06.

Every probabilistic formalism begins by declaring a measurable space. If the phenomenon of interest is the historical production of what is intelligible at all, that declaration pre-empts the phenomenon. Candidate directions, none yet adequate: presheaves over a *growing* site; category-theoretic constructions where objects are added as they are constituted, with colimits as sedimentation; open-ended evolutionary formalisms built to handle "the adjacent possible" (Kauffman's problem, still unsolved); type theories in which new types are introduced by construction rather than selected from a universe.

**Why it is the top question:** it is the formal expression of the difference between history and mechanism. Everything else in the programme depends on the answer, and the answer is not currently known. It is a legitimate open problem in mathematics, not only in philosophy.

**Termination status:** FORMAL BOTTLENECK. The concept is coherent; no adequate mathematics has been identified.

## Q-02 — Can epoch boundaries be identified by non-FEP means, precisely enough to license intra-epochal FEP modelling?

**From:** K-005, S-05.

If FEP-style modelling is legitimate only within an epoch of stable `Ω`, then the boundaries must be detectable independently. Candidates: change-point detection on classification schemes (when do codebooks undergo non-incremental revision?); residual-category spikes preceding reclassification (`formalizations.md` F-05); torque accumulation. **Testable now, on existing data** — ICD revisions, census category changes, legal-status reforms, platform-policy rewrites. A negative result would be as informative as a positive one.

**Termination status:** EMPIRICAL. Runnable immediately.

## Q-03 — Is the contextuality obstruction invariant under change of the analyst's frame? `[DECIDES F-06]`

**From:** K-009, `formalizations.md` F-06-D.

If measured incommensurability between two institutional classifications changes when the analyst's own carving changes, then the sheaf construction is measuring the analyst, and Viveiros de Castro's objection is fatal. If it is invariant, the construction has a genuine relational object.

**This is decidable mathematics and should be settled before further philosophy.** It also has a purely formal version: under what conditions is the obstruction class stable under refinement of the cover?

**Termination status:** FORMAL, then EMPIRICAL. Priority 1 for Cycle 2 alongside Q-01.

---

## Q-04 — Are legibility and colonization empirically separable?

**From:** `survivors.md` S-03, `dead_ends.md` D-07.

The theory says yes: uniform imposed categories with intact contestable reason-giving is one pathology; unarguable decisions within familiar categories is another. Find the four cells. The off-diagonal cases — high legibility with intact `R`, low legibility with `S`-coordination — are the ones that would confirm the distinction is real rather than an artefact of the theoretical apparatus. Administrative appeals data across jurisdictions with differing procedural requirements is the natural site.

**Consequence if separable:** "explainability" is exposed as a remedy addressed to the wrong mechanism, which is a publishable and policy-relevant result.

**Termination status:** EMPIRICAL. The most tractable question in the list.

---

## Q-05 — What distinguishes *domination* from *ordinary asymmetric coupling*?

**From:** K-008, S-07. The unresolved normative question underneath everything.

Every FEP description of an asymmetric relation is available as a description of homeostasis: the more powerful party is minimising surprise, the less powerful is adapting. The formalism has no place to record that one of these is a wrong. **Persistence-as-optimisation is a normatively anaesthetic vocabulary**, and this is the precise sense in which the framework can naturalise domination — not by endorsing it but by having no term for it.

The candidate differentia from S-07 clause (iii) — that the residue is rendered *nonexistent* rather than *unrecorded* — is the best available and is still not obviously normative rather than descriptive. **Where does the normative content enter, and can any formalism carry it, or must it always be supplied from outside?** The suspicion that it must always be supplied from outside is, if true, an important constraint on the entire enterprise.

**Termination status:** UNRESOLVED — genuinely open, and the best candidate for a Cycle 2 dialectical cycle in its own right.

---

## Q-06 — What makes a critical theory operationalisable by its target?

**From:** K-010, `dead_ends.md` D-09.

Reformulated from the Karp biography, where it was a piece of irony, into a general question about critique. Some critical concepts appear to convert readily into instruments (aggression as boundary-mediator; in-group/out-group dynamics; the diagnosis of what legitimates authority). Others resist (immanent critique; determinate negation; the standpoint of the classified). **Is there a structural property distinguishing them?**

Working conjecture, to be attacked: concepts that describe *mechanisms* are operationalisable by anyone; concepts that require occupying the *standpoint of the subordinated* are not, because occupying it is not a technique. If true, this predicts which parts of critical theory will be absorbed by the institutions they criticise — and it would explain the recurring pattern of critique becoming management vocabulary.

**Termination status:** GENERATIVE. High value, currently under-specified.

## Q-07 — Does the technology transform what agencies can intend, or supply capacity for pre-existing intent?

**From:** `claims.md` C-15.

Two causal claims with the same observables and different remedies. Under "capacity," the remedy is political and legal constraint on the agency. Under "transformation," the remedy must also target the technology's ontology. The source paper asserts transformation; the evidence offered supports capacity. Discriminating evidence: does the *category structure* of enforcement change after adoption — new target classes, new thresholds, new kinds of case — or only its *volume and speed*? That distinction is visible in enforcement records.

**Termination status:** EMPIRICAL BOTTLENECK. Argument cannot settle it.

## Q-10 — Could an AI system be built to *preserve* its contestation surface?

**From:** `survivors.md` S-09. The design consequence, and the only place in this cycle where the programme becomes constructive rather than diagnostic.

Current classification systems minimise the contestation surface: residual categories are collapsed, disagreement is treated as label noise, front-line discretion is engineered out as inconsistency, and refusals are recorded as missing data. A system built the other way would treat **inter-annotator disagreement as signal about `Ω`'s inadequacy rather than as noise**, would preserve rather than resolve residual categories, and would make its own torque legible to the classified.

**This is a concrete answer to the source paper's closing question** — what an immanent critique of AI using the tools of AI looks like — and it is buildable. Whether it is *critique* in Lukács's sense, or a more sophisticated form of the contemplative stance, is exactly K-006 reappearing at the level of design, and should be attacked in Cycle 2 rather than assumed.

# CYCLE 2 ADDITIONS

## Q-11 — Does explicitness without transferred authority produce any type-level revision? `[DECIDES K-011]`

**From:** `contradictions.md` K-011, the single stable contradiction remaining.

Making the frame explicit is either the precondition of contestation (A) or a substitute for it (B). This is decidable empirically: **compare institutions that published their classification schemes, model cards, ontologies or decision criteria against those that did not, and count actual revisions of `κ` initiated by or attributable to the classified population.**

If explicitness without transferred authority produces no type-level revisions, B wins decisively and **the entire transparency family of remedies — disclosure, explainability, model cards, algorithmic impact assessments — is exposed as level-2 legal endogeneity**: the disclosure functioning as the remedy.

**Termination status:** EMPIRICAL. High stakes, tractable, and directly policy-relevant. **New priority 1 alongside Q-01.**

## Q-12 — Test the F-09 anti-correlation on a real coarsening event

**From:** S-11, `formalizations.md` F-09. Prediction: across institutional consolidation, contextuality falls and residual load rises, with a sharper transition than either series alone shows.

Binding constraint, and it is interesting rather than fatal: **the losing regime's records are typically what consolidation destroys.** Sites where both survive — parallel customary/statutory tenure registries, dual diagnostic coding periods, staggered platform-policy harmonisation — are the feasible cases. **Where records do not survive, their destruction is itself the datum**, and the destruction is usually datable.

**Termination status:** EMPIRICAL. The cycle's one new falsifiable prediction.

## Q-13 — Is there any formal system with autonomous criterion revision?

**From:** S-14. FEP has heteronomous criterion revision at every non-top level and autonomous revision at none — the hierarchy pushes the fixed functional upward without eliminating it.

Is this specific to FEP or general to optimisation-based formalisms? Candidate places to look: fixed-point and self-referential constructions; systems whose objective is defined by their own trajectory rather than given in advance; open-ended evolutionary formalisms with no exogenous fitness. **Conjecture to attack: any formalism with a well-defined optimand has a fixed top-level criterion, and therefore no formalism of that class can represent autonomy in Hegel's sense.**

If the conjecture holds, it is a **general result about the limits of optimisation-based social modelling**, not a fact about FEP — and S-14's inversion generalises with it: this whole family of formalisms is native to heteronomy.

**Termination status:** FORMAL. Closely related to Q-01 and possibly the same question wearing different clothes.

## Q-14 — Which parts of critical theory are `T₂`-preserving and which are `T₁`-absorbable?

**From:** Q-06 sharpened by S-13. Q-06 conjectured that concepts describing *mechanisms* are operationalisable by anyone while concepts requiring the *standpoint of the subordinated* are not. The token/type distinction gives that conjecture a testable edge: **concepts that can be discharged by a procedure are absorbable; concepts that require transferring revisionary authority are not.**

Prediction: "transparency," "fairness," "explainability," "bias," "accountability" and "participation" are all `T₁`-discharge­able and will be absorbed as compliance functions. "Determinate negation," "immanent critique" and "the standpoint of the classified" are not, and will remain outside institutional adoption. **This is checkable against the actual trajectory of AI ethics vocabulary over the last decade**, and the pattern appears to hold, which would be a striking retrodiction.

**Termination status:** EMPIRICAL and immediately checkable. The highest generativity-per-effort question in the file.

## Q-15 — What distinguishes empire from standardisation? `[CYCLE 3 FOCAL]`

**From:** `claims.md` C-18 and its self-declared scandal. The composed epistemic definition of empire — enforced coarsening, residue rendered nonexistent, `T₂` absent, frame presenting as discovery — contains no violence, extraction or accumulation, and therefore does not currently distinguish the Colonial Office from ISO.

Two defences to attack: **(a)** the epistemic conditions are the differentia of the administrative form and presuppose extraction as genus (weak — makes the account an addendum); **(b)** the coarsening is the *mechanism* by which extraction becomes routine and deniable — it converts violence into administration, which is why empires produce paperwork.

**(b) makes a datable historical prediction: coarsening precedes or accompanies the stabilisation of extraction, never follows it.** Cadastral survey relative to dispossession; census and classification relative to taxation and conscription; standardised nomenclature relative to concession. **If coarsening reliably follows extraction, (b) is dead and the epistemic account is a description of empire's bookkeeping rather than of empire.**

**Termination status:** HISTORICAL / EMPIRICAL, and answerable from existing scholarship before any new data is touched. **Priority 1 for Cycle 3.**

## Q-16 — Whose cover produced the data? `[BLOCKING — must be answered before any dataset is used]`

**From:** S-11 and S-12 applied to method rather than to objects.

By S-11, a consolidated administrative corpus is a **single coarsened cover**. Running the apparatus on it will drive the contextuality obstruction to zero *by construction*, and reporting that as commensurability would be the exact error the apparatus exists to detect. **Analysing empire with data empire produced means working inside empire's cover.**

This does not make administrative data useless — F-09 says the loss relocates to residuals, and **residuals are visible in the coarsening regime's own records.** So the apparatus splits:

- **Residuality half** — F-05 (carving, residual load, torque), F-08 (`R`/`S` at decision sites), F-10 (`T₁`/`T₂`, revision authority). **Runs on a single regime's records.** Requires: category schemes, revision histories with initiators, residual-category counts over time, appeals and reason-giving records.
- **Cover half** — F-06 (contextuality), F-09 (anti-correlation across coarsening). **Requires two covers over the same population.** This is precisely what consolidation destroys.

**Methodological result — diachronic covers substitute for synchronic ones.** A single corpus with **version history** supplies its own second regime: an earlier schema is a different cover. Fields removed from a form, deprecated codes, merged categories, and collapsed enumerations are a **direct record of coarsening**. Schema deprecation history is the cover shrinking, written down by the coarsener.

**Four questions to ask of any well before use, in order:** (1) Who made it, for whom, and to settle what? (2) One regime or two? (3) Does it retain version history of its own categories? (4) Does it record what it refused, discarded, or could not classify?

Question (1) is the S-12 question and answering it is the first analytic act, not a preliminary.

**Termination status:** ~~BLOCKING~~ **DISCHARGED** against the Punjab print-register corpus (SV 412/44, 4,502 entries, 1910–1912). See `cycle3_corpus_encounter.md`. The corpus carries **both** halves: it is empire's carving apparatus preserved in operation, and it supplies three second covers — the gloss column (`φ` written down, per record), native-script/romanisation pairs, and annual drift in its own category vocabulary. The cover `𝓜` is **printed on the page** as `LANGUAGE—TOPIC` section headings, which discharges F-06's most contestable assumption from the source rather than by analyst declaration.

## Q-17 — Extractive vs. surveillant coarsening: do they leave different signatures? `[CYCLE 3, replaces the naive form of Q-15]`

**From:** `cycle3_corpus_encounter.md` §6. The Punjab register is a hard case for C-18 defence (b): conditions (i)–(iv) hold in full and **the extraction term is absent** — book registration takes nothing from printers. Act XXV of 1867 follows 1857; its function is intelligence, not revenue.

**Hypothesis (b″), to be attacked:** extractive and surveillant coarsening are two imperial modes with opposite documentary signatures.
- **Surveillant** coarsening wants to *understand* what it cannot classify → **high gloss rates, rich residual description, long hapax tails.**
- **Extractive** coarsening wants a *number* → **low gloss rates, thin residuals, forced assignment.**

The Punjab register is consistent with the surveillant arm: 96.4% vernacular gloss rate, and fifty language categories holding 408 entries. **An apparatus that documents its own classificatory failure in detail is doing something an extractive one has no reason to do.**

**Requires** a paired extractive register over an overlapping population — settlement reports, land-revenue records, or the *Punjab Alienation of Land Act* administrative categories — to test the other arm. Until then only half the hypothesis is testable.

**If (b″) holds,** C-18 survives with the genus split rather than weakened, and empire is distinguished from standardisation by *what the coarsening is for*, evidenced in the density of its own residual documentation. **If it fails,** C-18 must retreat to (b′) — genus = domination — and probably loses the ability to exclude ordinary bureaucracy, which would be fatal.

**Termination status:** EMPIRICAL, half-runnable now.

## Q-18 — Does the register's genre-vocabulary drift *because* a term is being contested?

**From:** `cycle3_handbill_trace.md` §4. `hand-bill` names the Punjab Religious Book Society's monthly series 1881–1893; ceases to be applied to that series by 1907 while the series continues; and reappears 1910–1930 attached to **Sikh, Ahmadi and intra-Sikh** publishers — including a body that named itself *The Sikh Hand Bill Committee, Lahore*.

**Hypothesis:** a genre word becomes unavailable to its originator at roughly the moment competitors adopt it, and the register's descriptive vocabulary tracks that contest.

**If true, the consequence is large:** the classification scheme is not merely failing to see the mobilisation — **it is being moved by it.** The register would then be a *participant* in the contest over what things are called, not an external observer of it, and every category in it becomes a datable artefact of a struggle rather than a colonial imposition simpliciter. That would substantially complicate C-18(iv) — "the frame presents as discovery rather than decision" — by showing the frame is also *reactive*.

**Testable:** track genre words (`tract`, `pamphlet`, `leaflet`, `hand-bill`, `ishtihar`, `risala`) by publisher and community across the 22 OCR-bearing volumes; look for handover events where a term's publisher-mix turns over within a few years.

**Termination status:** EMPIRICAL, runnable now on existing files, no extraction required.

## Q-19 — How much of the corpus is invisible, and to whom has it always been invisible? `[BLOCKING, and it is a finding]`

**1,755 pages — 17.2% of SV 412/44 — have no OCR text layer**: 1876–80, 1894–99, 1900–1903, 1904–06. A contiguous thirteen-year hole, 1894–1906, plus one earlier volume.

Detected by a control (English-word density per page), not by inspection. **Nothing in the filenames, page counts, file sizes or documentation announces it.** Every full-text claim ever made against this archive silently inherits the hole.

**Immediate actions:** (1) document it in the repo — it bounds Davis's work as much as ours; (2) check whether Library 2's copies of the same volumes have text layers (they may have been scanned separately); (3) treat those four volumes as an OCR workstream candidate — they are the highest-value extraction targets in the corpus precisely because no full-text method can currently reach them.

**Termination status:** BLOCKING for any longitudinal claim. Partly discharged by (2), which has not been checked.

## Cycle 3 agenda — but do not run it by argument

Cycle 2 terminated on convergence, conceptual transformation, and an empirical bottleneck. **Every remaining question is now either formal (Q-01, Q-13), empirical (Q-11, Q-12, Q-14, Q-02, Q-04, Q-07), or textual (Q-08, Q-09).** None is answerable by another dialectical round.

The single stable contradiction (K-011) has been shown to be one contradiction appearing at three scales rather than three separate ones. Restating it would be degenerative.

**The process has argued itself to the boundary of what argument can produce. Continuing is refusing the result.**
